issues.t: Balance shaft or timing idler gear wears out
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with camshaft timing codes P0016 or P0017. At first the light may come and go and the engine runs normally; later it stays on and the engine can shake or rattle.
issues.why: On many V6 and V8 engines built from about 2005 into 2007, a timing gear (the balance shaft sprocket on the V6, the idler gear on the V8) was made from metal that was too soft. Its teeth wear down, so the timing chain slips out of step with the crankshaft.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Mercedes dealer to check whether your engine serial number is in the affected range. Don't ignore it for long: if the teeth strip, the engine can be badly damaged. The repair is a big job, so get a firm quote.

issues.t: Harsh shifts, limp mode or fluid leak at the transmission plug
issues.sym: Hard or delayed shifts (often the 2-3 shift), slow engagement into Drive or Reverse, or the car getting stuck in 2nd gear with little power. Some cars show transmission fluid around the wiring plug on the side of the gearbox.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic uses a circuit board inside the gearbox (the conductor plate) with speed sensors that fail with age. The plug where the wiring enters the case can also leak fluid, which can creep up the harness toward the control unit. Old or low fluid makes shifting worse.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned for codes and check the fluid level and condition. A leaking plug is cheap to reseal; a failed conductor plate can often be replaced without rebuilding the whole gearbox.

issues.t: Engine stalls or won't restart when hot (crank sensor)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving and then won't restart until it cools down, or it cranks for a long time before starting. Stalling at idle can happen too.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor tells the engine computer where the crankshaft is. When it starts to fail, usually with heat, the computer loses that signal and shuts off spark and fuel.
issues.next: If the engine stalls, get safely off the road. Have the codes read; this sensor is a common and fairly cheap part on these engines and is often the first thing to check.

issues.t: Misfire from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: Rough idle (often worst when cold), a loss of power when accelerating, a flashing or steady check engine light with misfire codes, and sometimes a fuel smell.
issues.why: The ignition coils on this V6 wear out with heat and age. This engine also has two spark plugs per cylinder, so worn plugs add to the strain on the coils.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find which coil is weak. Many shops replace the coils and all 12 spark plugs together. Avoid cheap no-name coils.

issues.t: Worn engine and transmission mounts
issues.sym: Strong vibration in the cabin at idle, a thump when shifting into Drive or Reverse, or a clunk when you get on and off the gas.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts soften and sag with age and heat, so they no longer soak up engine movement.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked with the hood open while someone shifts between Drive and Reverse. Replace worn mounts in pairs so the engine sits level.

issues.t: Mass airflow sensor fails
issues.sym: Hesitation or stumbling when accelerating, rough running, poor fuel economy and often a check engine light.
issues.why: The mass airflow sensor measures the air going into the engine. Its sensing element gets dirty or fails with age, so the engine gets the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Check that the air filter is clean, and fit a new filter when the sensor is replaced. Use a genuine or quality sensor.

issues.t: Front control arm and thrust arm bushings crack
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps or when braking, vague or wandering steering, the car pulling to one side, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front control arms and thrust (tension) arms crack and wear out. Some are oil-filled and leak when they fail.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replace worn arms or bushings and then get a wheel alignment.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends and suspension joints
issues.sym: Knocking or looseness in the steering, wandering on the highway, and tires wearing on the edges.
issues.why: Tie rod ends, ball joints and other suspension joints wear with mileage and rough roads. Worn joints and bushings are the most common inspection failure on these cars in UK testing data.
issues.next: Have the steering and suspension joints checked for play. Replace worn parts and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Power window regulator fails
issues.sym: A window that moves slowly, makes grinding or clicking noises, drops into the door, or won't go up at all. On convertibles, a stuck window can also stop the top from working.
issues.why: The window regulator uses cables and plastic slides that stretch, crack or come loose with age. The driver's window and the rear windows on convertibles wear out most.
issues.next: If a window won't close, cover it to keep rain out and have the regulator replaced. After repair, the window and top may need to be reset with a scan tool.

issues.t: ABS and ESP warning lights from a bad brake light switch
issues.sym: The ABS, ESP or brake warning lights come on, brake lights may stay on or not work, and cruise control may stop working.
issues.why: The brake light switch at the brake pedal wears out. The stability control system uses its signal, so a faulty switch turns on several warning lights at once.
issues.next: Have the codes read before replacing larger parts. The brake light switch is cheap and quick to replace, and working brake lights matter for safety.

issues.t: ABS control unit fails
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights stay on, and ABS may not work in a hard stop.
issues.why: The ABS control unit (modulator) can fail internally. Old brake fluid that has absorbed water is a known cause of this failure.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The brakes still work without ABS, but drive gently and get it repaired soon. Change the brake fluid every two years to protect the new unit.

issues.t: Check engine light from secondary air injection faults
issues.sym: A check engine light with secondary air system codes. The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The secondary air system pumps air into the exhaust for a short time after a cold start to warm up the catalytic converters. Its pump, valves and hoses fail with age.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the system tested. It is not urgent for the engine, but the car will fail an emissions test with the light on.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or fuel pump fails
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads empty after filling up, sticks at full, or jumps around; in some cases the engine stalls or won't start because the pump has failed.
issues.why: The fuel level sending units in the tank wear out, and the fuel pump can fail with age. Owners of both generations report replacing these parts.
issues.next: Use the trip meter to track fuel until the gauge is fixed so you don't run out. Have the sender and pump tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Air conditioning blows warm
issues.sym: Weak or warm air from the vents, or cold air only on one side.
issues.why: Common causes are a refrigerant leak at the receiver-drier hose, a failed evaporator temperature sensor, a stuck blend door actuator, and on high-mileage cars a worn compressor.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked for leaks and codes before recharging it. Recharging without fixing a leak wastes money.

issues.t: Headlight wiring insulation breaks down
issues.sym: Headlights flicker, stop working or trigger bulb warnings, and the wiring near the headlights looks cracked or brittle.
issues.why: The insulation on the headlight wiring harness breaks down with heat and age, exposing wires that can short.
issues.next: Have the headlight wiring inspected. Replace the damaged harness rather than taping it, since bare wires can short out.

issues.t: Rust, including front spring perches that can break
issues.sym: Rust bubbles on fender edges, door bottoms, sills and wheel arches. If a front spring perch breaks, you may hear a loud bang or clunk and see one front corner drop, with the tire rubbing the fender.
issues.why: This generation used water-based paint and had little rust protection. Salt and water attack the welds that hold the front spring perches to the inner fenders.
issues.next: Have the body and the front spring perches inspected, especially in snowy or wet climates. A cracked perch is a safety problem and should be repaired or reinforced before more driving.

issues.t: Convertible top leaks hydraulic fluid or stops working
issues.sym: The top moves slowly, stops partway or won't move. You may find hydraulic fluid in the trunk or behind the rear seats, damp carpets after rain, or a soft-top warning light.
issues.why: The top is moved by hydraulic rams whose seals wear out after about 15 years. Cables, position switches and a sensor in the windshield latch can also fail.
issues.next: Don't keep cycling a top that is leaking fluid. Have a convertible specialist find the leaking ram or failed switch; rebuilding rams is often cheaper than buying new ones.

issues.t: Intake manifold flaps break off
issues.sym: A check engine light, rough running or a rattle from the top of the engine. In bad cases broken plastic pieces get sucked into the engine.
issues.why: Plastic flaps inside the intake manifold, which change the air path for more power, get brittle with age and can break.
issues.next: Have the intake manifold flaps inspected at high mileage, especially if you hear rattling. Fix it soon, because broken pieces can damage the engine.

issues.t: Instrument cluster display loses pixels
issues.sym: Missing lines or segments in the display that shows the odometer, outside temperature and messages, making it hard to read.
issues.why: The LCD screen in the instrument cluster ages and loses pixels. In some cases a burned-out backlight bulb is the real cause.
issues.next: Check the backlight bulbs first. A cluster repair specialist can usually fix the display for less than a new cluster.

issues.t: Fuel pump may keep running after a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in everyday driving. The risk only shows up after a collision, when the fuel pump could keep running and feed a fuel leak.
issues.why: A software calibration fault could leave the fuel pump powered after a crash, raising the risk of fire. Mercedes-Benz recalled affected cars (campaign 2008 070001) and reprograms the software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls at a Mercedes-Benz dealer or on the NHTSA site and have the free software update done.
